newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields ended the week on a firmer note. A stronger crown and falling debt yields by other high-yielders helped fuel the trend and the undertone was positive, dealers said.
The Swedish market was seen remaining bullish. Tuesday's Federal Reserve meeting was in focus and would probably dictate moves next week.
"Sweden is starting up a positive spiral," one dealer said.
Nine year bond yields fell eight basis points to 7.62 percent. Four year bond yields closed seven basis points lower at 6.53 percent.
The budget posed few surprises and was well received. "The positive thing is that they now have a target of achieving a budget surplus in 1999," Peter Lindqvist of HSBC Midland said.
The spread between Swedish and German long yields narrowed another five basis points to 146 and dealers said this trend would probably continue.

The crown remained strong compared to a generally weaker mark and flirted with the resistance level of 4.3500 against the mark. The mark softened to 4.3610 crowns compared to 4.3775 crowns late Thursday and more gains were seen ahead.
